input: Most people think of sourdough as a difficult bread, but the process is mostly waiting. You mix the dough, let it rest, fold it a few times, and then leave it alone overnight. The starter does the real work, slowly fermenting the flour and giving the bread it's sour flavor. The hardest part is learning to read the dough instead of the clock, since temperature and humidity change everything. Once you get a feel for it, you'll find it alot easier than it looks.

input: Tomatoes are one of the easiest vegetables to grow at home, as long as they get enough sun. Aim for at least six hours of direct light a day, and water deeply a few times a week rather than a little every day. Shallow watering encourages shallow roots, which makes the plants more sensative to heat. Once the first fruits appear, its a good idea to add a layer of mulch to keep the soil moist.

input: Code review is less about catching bugs than about sharing context. When I review a pull request, I'm mostly trying to understand why the change was made and whether it fits with the rest of the system. Bugs do get caught, of course, but the bigger payoff is that two people now understand the code instead of one. That redundancy pays off the first time someone is on vacation and there feature breaks in production. It's also the cheapest form of mentorship I know of, especially for newer engineers who arent sure what good looks like yet.

input: This change adress the memory leak in the image processing worker. The worker was holding onto references to every proccessed file, so memory usage grew untill the pod got OOM-killed. I refactered the loop so each buffer is released after it's upload completes. Memory now stays flat at around 300 MB through out a full run. Their are still a few optimizations we could make, but I'd rather ship this fix first.

acceptableOutputs: This change addresses the memory leak in the image processing worker. The worker was holding onto references to every processed file, so memory usage grew until the pod got OOM-killed. I refactored the loop so each buffer is released after its upload completes. Memory now stays flat at around 300 MB throughout a full run. There are still a few optimizations we could make, but I'd rather ship this fix first.
